summary: Sally McAra specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), supervised by Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.

Sally Mellick Cutler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford by 1993. She served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1996–1997).

Salomon Lefmann (1831–1912) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and completed his Ph.D. at Berlin. He taught at Heidelberg University from 1866, becoming an associate professor in 1870 and honorary professor in 1901.

Saloni Mathur works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, including Associate Professor of Art History (attested 2011) and Professor and Chair of Art History (attested 2026).

Sam van Schaik (born 1972) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Manchester, held a post at SOAS, and was appointed Head of the Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library in 1999.
Samani Pratibha Pragya is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she also worked as a research assistant (attested 2020).
Sambhavi Ganesh works in Indology. As attested in 2026, she has pursued doctoral studies at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Radhika Govinda.

Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti (born 1940) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He has held positions at the University of Calcutta and at The Asiatic Society, where he served as Professor (Special Invitee) as attested in 2026.
Sampan Chakrabarty works in Indology. As attested in 2026, he has been a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society and a doctoral student under Pallab Sengupta.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay (born 1936) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar educated at Drepung Monastery, SOAS, and the University of London. He served as CNRS Directeur de Recherche (1980) and President of the IATS (1995–2000).

Samuel Beal (1825–1889) was a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Trinity College, Cambridge, and Durham University. He was appointed Professor of Chinese at University College London in 1877 and held a post at the University of London.

Samuel George Frederick Brandon (1907–1971) was a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leeds (circa 1930–1934) and held a post at the University of Manchester from around 1951 to 1971.
Samuel Johnson (1709–1784) was a scholar in linguistics. He was educated at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge (circa 1725–1726), and Pembroke College, Oxford (1728–1731).
Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Central Asian, Sinological, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.

Samuel Wells Williams (1812–1884) was a Sinologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (circa 1831–1832). He later held an academic post at Yale University from circa 1877 to 1884.

Sandra A. Wawrytko works in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held faculty positions at San Diego State University, serving as Professor (attested 1999) and Associate Professor of Philosophy (attested 2014).
Sandra Bell is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and subsequently held a post there.
Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she was supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes and taught by Anne MacDonald.
Sang-Kyun Sun works in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Delhi under Sanghasen Singh and served as a lecturer at JinGak Buddhist College (both attested 1995).

Sangay Dorji is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies educated at Tengtho Monastery and Semtokha Rigney School. He taught at Semtokha Rigney School and served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission (attested 1999–2004).
